notable_absence.finding: Only ONE of roughly ninety documented settings on this page carries an edition badge (use_fts). Two more state an edition-dependent ceiling in prose rather than as a badge (queryNumCpus/num-cpus and queryMaxParallelism/max-parallelism, both capped at 4 cores in Community Edition). Everything else is silent on edition. Separately, there is no predicate in the registry for the 'all four or none' mutual-requirement constraint that binds natural/natural_cred/natural_orgid/natural_context ('If you don't specify all four parameters, the Query Service returns an error'). requiresSetting was used four times to approximate it, but that loses the fact that the requirement is symmetric and total; reconciliation may want a mutuallyRequiredWith or requiresAllOf predicate.

cross_product_finding: The Capella twin (cloud/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-settings.md) documents ONLY the request-level parameters. All of 'Overview', 'How Setting Levels Interact', 'All Query Settings' (Tables 1-5), 'Cluster-Level Query Settings' (with its Access sub-object for queryCurlWhitelist) and 'Node-Level Query Settings' (with Logging Parameters and the Plan Qualifier) are Server-only - a ~290-line block with no Capella counterpart, because cluster-level and node-level settings are not tenant-visible on Capella. Two more precise divergences worth recording as identity-distinguishing evidence: (1) The use_fts row carries '[ENTERPRISE EDITION](https://www.couchbase.com/products/editions)' on the Server page and NO badge at all on the Capella page - correct, because Capella has no Community Edition, but it means the same parameter is edition-gated in one product and unconditional in the other. Do not merge into a single unconditional concept. (2) The Community-Edition core caps for num_cpus and max_parallelism are present in the Server prose and entirely absent from the Capella page ('Community Edition' does not appear anywhere in cloud/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-settings.md). Conversely, the Capella page retains every literal 'Couchbase Server X.Y and later' gate verbatim (already flagged by the Capella extraction), so the version vocabulary is the same on both sides even though the edition vocabulary is not.
version_finding: This is the richest version-gating page in the batch: seven distinct version gates at four different granularities. (1) Five parameters gated at 8.0 (natural, natural_cred, natural_orgid, natural_context, natural_output) using a two-part convention - a bare 'Couchbase Server 8.0' badge immediately after the parameter name, PLUS the prose sentence 'This parameter is available in clusters running Couchbase Server 8.0 and later.' natural_output has the badge and prose but omits the 'To use this parameter you must also specify...' clause its four siblings carry, which is arguably an inconsistency since it is equally part of the all-four set. (2) One capability gated at minor version 7.6.0 (read from replica) - and note it is phrased as a property of the CLUSTER ('Reading from replica is only possible if the cluster uses Couchbase Server 7.6.0 or later'), not of the parameter, which matters for whether availableSince attaches to the setting or to the feature. (3) Two gated at PATCH level: 7.6.4 (completed-stream-size) and 7.6.8 (parameter masking). Any version concept scheme must therefore accept three-part versions - version:server-7-6-8 style - not just major.minor. (4) One deprecation at 6.5 (encoded_plan), which is the only deprecation evidence in this batch and is expressed in the weakest possible form: the word 'deprecated' appears only as a parenthetical in the Table 2 summary list with no version attached, while the row itself says only that the parameter 'is ignored and has no effect' from 6.5 onward. There is no removal date, no 'use X instead', and no statement of what replaced it. This is precisely the vocabulary gap the wave is chasing: the docs distinguish 'announced deprecated' from 'became a no-op' from 'removed' only by accident of wording, so a single deprecatedIn predicate will flatten a real distinction. Recommend reconciliation mint deprecatedIn plus a separate noOpSince (or ignoredSince) and removedIn. Finally, unrelated to gating: several cross-references on this 8.0 page are hard-coded absolute Server 8.0 URLs ('/server/8.0/learn/data/transactions.html', '/server/8.0/learn/data/durability.html') rather than relative links, which will rot at the next release.
